samples.summary: PUT validator now rejects one level more than the writer accepts, breaking GET→PUT identity for a max-nested document
samples.evidence: `assertValidBlock` increments `depth` only through `tableData.rows[].cells[].blocks[]` (line 502), so `depth` counts enclosing tables. The new `if (depth >= MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH)` rejects *any* block at depth 32 — including an ordinary paragraph inside a table that sits at depth 31. But depth 31 is the deepest table the readers materialize and `writeDocsRoot`/`documentHasTableAtNestingCap` explicitly allow (`hasDocsTableAtNestingCap` only trips on a *table* at depth >= 32, docs-tree.ts:236). So a document with 32 nested tables (depths 0…31) whose innermost cell holds text is written fine by `writeDocsRoot`, is returned in full by `readDocsRoot`/GET, yet its own body now 400s on PUT — the round-trip identity this file documents. The condition should be `depth > MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH`, or should key on `b.type === 'table'` the way the writer's check does.

samples.summary: `capTableNesting` short-circuits at baseDepth 0, so a top-level paste is never capped even though the doc-comment claims an absolute invariant
samples.evidence: `if (baseDepth <= 0) return blocks;` returns the fragment untouched whenever the paste target is at depth 0. The doc-comment above it says paste "owes the same absolute invariant" as the importer and the CRDT writers, but at depth 0 nothing is enforced: a fragment carrying >= 32 nested tables would land in the model unchecked, `insertBlockAt` → `buildBlockNode(block, 0)` would truncate the over-deep tables to rowless nodes in the CRDT while the local `Doc` model keeps their rows, and a later `writeFullDocument` on that model would throw. Today the only fragment sources are the JSON payload (bounded by `MAX_TABLE_DEPTH = 8`, line 72/309) and HTML (whose `parseHtmlTableElement` flattens nested tables), so it is not reachable — but the guard is one relaxed producer away from being wrong, and the invariant it documents does not hold as written.

samples.summary: New shared pointer-gesture resolver dereferences `targetCell.blocks[0].id` and calls throwing `doc.getBlock()` without guards, on a path shift+click now reaches for the first time
samples.evidence: `resolveCellGesture` guards `!targetCell` but then reads `targetCell.blocks[0].id` (lines 4047 and 4066) — a cell with an empty `blocks` array is a TypeError. It also calls `this.doc.getBlock(anchorTableId)` (4031) and `this.doc.getBlock(resolveTableId)` (4055), which *throw* `Block not found` rather than returning undefined when the `blockParentMap` entry is stale. The drag path already had these dereferences, but the shift+click branch (line 2144) did not: it previously only called `resolveOffsetInCell` and fell through to a caret move. So a stale parent map or a block-less cell now turns a shift+click into an uncaught throw out of the mousedown handler where it used to just move the caret.

samples.summary: `Math.max(1, ...cells.map(...))` (and the same spread in `parseHtmlTableElement`) can RangeError on a clipboard-sized row count — the exact hazard this change folds away elsewhere
samples.evidence: `pasteTableCells` computes `const cols = Math.max(1, ...cells.map(r => r.length));` over clipboard-supplied rows, and `parseHtmlTableElement` does `const maxCols = Math.max(...rows.map(r => r.length));` (clipboard.ts:891). Both spread an attacker/paste-controlled array into an argument list, which throws `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded` past ~100k entries. This change explicitly folds two other instances of that exact pattern for that exact reason (`range-slices.ts:56-60` and `selection.ts`'s new `maxCol` reduce), but left these two — and `pasteTableCells` is a function the change otherwise edits.

mergedFrom.summary: The new paste/insert nesting guards read `Doc.tableNestingDepth`, which is backed by the layout-time `blockParentMap` and is documented to be stale for blocks created since the last layout — the cap then silently reads 0

finding.summary: New read-time truncation creates `tableData.rows === []` blocks that navigation code dereferences unguarded
finding.evidence: The change makes every reader materialize a table at `MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH` as `{ ...tableData, rows: [] }` (crdt-tree.ts `treeNodeToBlock`: `depth >= MAX ? [] : ...`; yorkie-doc-store.ts line ~568 likewise). That block shape did not exist before this change. Multiple consumers assume a table block always has at least one row+cell+block: `text-editor.ts:4911` and `:4929` (`nextBlock.tableData.rows[0].cells[0].blocks[0].id` in `moveRight`), `:5142`, `:5177`, `:4743`, `:3223`. Arrow-navigating into a truncated table throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'cells')`. `handleArrow` reportedly catches throws as "stale layout", but `moveRight`/`moveDown` are reached from other callers too. The truncation is deliberate; the unguarded consumers were never updated to expect it.

verdict.reason: The finding claims text-editor.ts navigation consumers dereference `tableData.rows[0].cells[0].blocks[0]` unguarded for reader-truncated rowless tables. That code is not present. Every table-entry path in text-editor.ts routes through the helpers `firstCellBlock` (:77-81, `block.tableData?.rows[0]?.cells`, returns undefined) and `lastCellBlock` (:87-95, `rows?.[rows.length - 1]`, returns undefined), with `?? fallbackBlock` or `if (entered)` at each call site: moveRight :4980 and :4998, moveLeft :4937 and :4956, arrow up/down table entry :3175, :3203, :3275, :3303, page-boundary/vertical :5208-5209 and :5251-5252, and lastPositionInCell :3943-3950 (`if (!entered) break;`). The only direct rows[0] reads in the file are optional-chained with fallbacks (:4811, :5920). Cited line :3223 contains no table dereference at all, and moveRight is at :4964, not :4911. A dedicated regression suite (test/view/rowless-table-nav.test.ts:118-192) drives ArrowRight/ArrowLeft/Shift+Tab into a `rows: []` table and asserts no throw plus correct caret landing. The only unguarded `rows[0].cells[0].blocks[0]` reads found anywhere (editor.ts:4246, :4271) operate on tables just created locally by insertTable/insertTableInCell, behind the depth check at editor.ts:4232 — not the truncated-read path the finding describes.
